title: Interleaved KV segment donation and prefetch timeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Under sustained token streaming workloads, our paged KV cache exhibits tail latency spikes when multiple large sequences evict overlapping resident segments. Root cause analysis points to contention in the residency donor path and imprecise prefetch timing: the system either prefetches too late (causing blocking GPU paging) or too early (wasting bandwidth and evicting useful entries).
background: Current implementation uses slab-style blocks and a global eviction marker. Batches request KV pages synchronously when a miss occurs, resulting in uncoordinated GPU memory churn. Recent incidents (see ENG-91234 and ENG-94822) show 99.9th percentile latency regressions during mixed short/long session traffic and when autoscaling creates transient load bursts.
goal: Design and implement an interleaved segment donation protocol with a bounded prefetch timeline that coordinates donations across concurrent batch streams, reduces duplicate prefetches, and supports graceful demotion of segments to host memory without violating latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: P99 token generation latency no worse than current baseline under representative burst tests (within 5%)
Median token throughput improved or unchanged for mixed-length workloads
GPU memory churn (pages moved per minute) reduced by >=30% in synthetic overlap tests
No regression in deterministic unit tests; e2e harness validates under 3 load shapes and two model sizes
Monitoring: new metrics emitted for segment_donations, coordinated_prefetches, duplicate_prefetch_rate
implementation_plan: Design: define segment donorship semantics and bounded donation window (0.5 - 2.0s adjustable)
Instrumentation: add lightweight donation intents and prefetch tokens to trace spans
Coordinator: implement per-GPU coordinator that serializes donation leaders per-stripe to avoid concurrent swaps of adjacent segments
Prefetch manager: bounded timeline with backoff and cancellation if leader donation completes
Batch integration: propagate donation hints in batch headers to allow early pipelined prefetching
Testing: unit tests for donation state machine; integration tests with multi-worker harness; canary on dedicated pool
Rollout: shadow traffic for two days, canary 5% traffic then 25% then full once metrics stable
risks: Coordinator becomes a single point of contention under very high concurrency—mitigate by sharding coordinators by token affinity
Incorrect bounded window tuning could either cause too-early prefetching (wasted bandwidth) or too-late prefetching (latency spikes)
More complex state machine increases maintenance burden; need clear invariants and safety timeouts
Edge cases with model kv layout permutations may require per-model tuning
benchmarks: Local benchmark (small model): duplicate_prefetch_rate reduced from 18% -> 4% in overlap test
Staging load test (gpt-medium equivalent): GPU page moves/min reduced 38% with coordinator enabled
Latency: P99 increased 2.2% in worst-case synthetic blast but improved 12% in typical mixed workloads
notes: Trade-off: prefer slightly more prefetching for short sequences to avoid blocking latency at the expense of some extra host->GPU bandwidth
Pinned decision: donation leader chosen by batch timestamp + stripe id to make selection deterministic and debuggable
We will expose donation_window_ms as a runtime knob controlled in console for dedicated/private customers
